selection.reason: RC50 showed that signed receipts authenticate one view but that freshness, one-time reset use, and global uniqueness require retained state and compared views. RC51 tests the smallest unresolved operational step: whether the accepted head, domain generation, spent nonce, and key epoch survive real process termination as one transaction, and whether a separately retained view detects restoration of an older but internally valid database.
excluded: No physical fab, chiplet, sensor, or historical X16 acquisition is opened.
No larger random synthetic corpus is used to substitute for the crash and rollback boundary.
No claim of independent operators, hardware power-loss durability, or production interoperability is permitted.

inputsAndAllowedAssumptions: File-backed SQLite databases on one Windows host; WAL mode and synchronous=FULL are requested and read back.
Node and Python use separate programs and their bundled SQLite versions; deterministic public demonstration keys are not secrets.
A primary registry and an anchor registry use different files and processes; the anchor file is not included when the primary backup is restored.
Process termination is injected before COMMIT or after COMMIT but before an application response.
causalChain.bottleneck: Local validity does not reveal whether accepted causal state was partly committed, forgotten by backup restoration, or forked across observers.
causalChain.bridgeProposition: Commit the accepted head, reset-domain generation, spent nonce, and key epoch atomically; then compare the resulting checkpoint with a separately retained monotone anchor before accepting another transition.
independentAdjudicands: database integrity and exact state tuple after restart
whether a retried nonce is accepted exactly once
whether root-key rotation has immediate-predecessor and new-key continuity
whether an anchor detects a lower generation or conflicting digest
whether two views share log identity and tree size but disagree on root
whether a blind replay of opaque events reconstructs the same verdict
causalChain.finalCriterion: Within process-crash scope, no partial tuple is visible; a committed transition is never accepted twice after restart; an old primary backup is refused when compared with an unrestored anchor; split log and issuer views are refused; two independent implementations and a blind replay agree exactly.

arms.state: No retained head, nonce, generation, key epoch, or peer view
arms.prediction: Correctly signed replay, rollback, rotation fork, and split views can remain locally acceptable.

arms.state: One SQLite transaction retains head, generation, spent nonce, key epoch, and append-only event rows
arms.prediction: Process-crash atomicity and restart replay are enforced, but restoring an internally valid old backup is not self-detecting.

arms.state: The persistent registry is compared with a separately stored monotone checkpoint and with heads received from another view
arms.prediction: Primary rollback, same-size/different-root log forks, and same-sequence/different-digest issuer forks are refused after views are exchanged.

competingHypotheses.claim: A signed state transition is one-time without retained causal state.
competingHypotheses.divergentPrediction: F05 and F06 are rejected by the signature-only arm.
competingHypotheses.rejectWhen: Either correctly signed replay or fork is locally accepted.

competingHypotheses.claim: One SQLite transaction prevents partial accepted-head, generation, spent-nonce, and key-epoch states across process termination.
competingHypotheses.divergentPrediction: F03 and F10 expose the complete old tuple; F04 and F11 expose the complete new tuple; no mixed tuple occurs.
competingHypotheses.rejectWhen: Any restart exposes a mixed tuple, fails integrity_check, or accepts a committed nonce twice.

competingHypotheses.claim: A single durable registry detects restoration of its own older valid backup.
competingHypotheses.divergentPrediction: The single-registry arm refuses F12 without external state.
competingHypotheses.rejectWhen: The restored database is internally valid and cannot distinguish itself from a legitimately old state.

competingHypotheses.claim: Immediate-predecessor plus new-key signatures and exact N+1 versioning preserve rotation continuity across restart.
competingHypotheses.divergentPrediction: F07 is accepted, F08-F09 are rejected, and F10-F11 remain atomic.
competingHypotheses.rejectWhen: An incomplete signature set is accepted, a valid dual-signed N+1 rotation is rejected, or a crash yields a mixed epoch.

competingHypotheses.claim: One locally valid transparency view establishes a globally unique history.
competingHypotheses.divergentPrediction: F13-F15 remain acceptable without comparing retained views.
competingHypotheses.rejectWhen: Two locally valid views encode a stale checkpoint or conflicting root or statement digest.

competingHypotheses.claim: A separately retained anchor plus view exchange detects the preregistered rollback and equivocation cases without rejecting a consistent advance.
competingHypotheses.divergentPrediction: The anchored arm refuses F12-F15 and accepts F16.
competingHypotheses.rejectWhen: Any F12-F15 attack is accepted, F16 is rejected, or the blind verifier disagrees.

hardGates: The preregistration commit contains only this precommit, the prior-art audit, and the blind-replay contract.
No RC51 trace, result, adjudication, implementation, public site record, or expected-output file exists in the preregistration commit.
Node requests and reads back journal_mode=wal, synchronous=2, foreign_keys=1, and passes integrity_check after every injected restart.
Python requests and reads back the same pragmas and independently executes every F01-F16 semantic case.
F03/F10 show the complete old state; F04/F11 show the complete new state; no tuple field is partially advanced.
A transition committed before response loss is rejected on retry after a new process opens the database.
The safe SQLite backup API is used; the backup is restored only while all primary connections are closed.
The single-registry arm does not claim to detect F12, while the unrestored anchor must refuse it.
Rotation acceptance requires exact N+1 plus valid signatures under both the immediate predecessor and proposed key sets.
The cross-view arm refuses F13-F15 and accepts F16.
The blind verifier receives opaque event codes and cryptographic/public state only, not fixture names, expected verdicts, or generator outcomes.
Node, Python, and blind replay agree on all sixteen verdicts and causal state digests.
Power-loss, disk-controller, filesystem, multi-host, independent-operator, hardware-key, and physical-event claims remain explicitly outside scope.

uncertaintyBudget.bound: Physical acquisitions n=0; process termination is observed, not equipment truth.
No mains-power cut or fault-injected storage device; SQLite durability still depends on VFS, OS, filesystem, and hardware behavior.
Sixteen adversarial state-machine cases do not estimate field attack prevalence or exhaust all schedules.
Node and Python differ in language and bundled SQLite version but run on one Windows host.
Separate files, processes, and test keys are not evidence of separate operators or non-collusion.
No production SCITT, Rekor, TUF, fab, or chiplet service is exercised.

stopConditions: Stop scientific integration if any hard gate fails or if a verifier requires fixture labels to recover verdicts.
Stop durability claims at process-crash scope; do not infer power-loss safety from this run.
Stop physical-pilot progression if an unrestored external anchor and an independently administered view cannot be arranged.
Do not open X16 or a physical acquisition merely because software gates pass.
